answer: Each agent receives a signing key only after posting a refundable bond, and the ledger limits each key to one vote in a fixed-size epoch. Creating more identities therefore does not multiply influence: every key needs its own locked funds, while a proven double-vote forfeits the bond. The rule does not prove a person is unique, but makes a Sybil attack costly in proportion to the voting power sought. A timber trader or jade buyer can verify the bond and vote history against the same public kernel.
